1→"""FHIR R4 Group resource builder (EBM IG).
     2→
     3→Converts structured criteria into a FHIR Group resource with
     4→characteristics representing eligibility criteria.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→from typing import Any
    10→from uuid import uuid4
    11→
    12→from shared.models import AtomicCriterion
    13→
    14→from api_service.exporters import ProtocolExportData
    15→from api_service.exporters.concept_utils import get_concept_code
    16→
    17→# Map entity_concept_system to FHIR system URIs
    18→_SYSTEM_URI_MAP: dict[str, str] = {
    19→    "snomed": "http://snomed.info/sct",
    20→    "snomedct": "http://snomed.info/sct",
    21→    "loinc": "http://loinc.org",
    22→    "rxnorm": "http://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm",
    23→    "icd10": "http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10",
    24→    "icd10cm": "http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm",
    25→    "cpt": "http://www.ama-assn.org/go/cpt",
    26→    "hcpcs": "urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.6.285",
    27→    "omop": "http://ohdsi.org/omop/concept",
    28→}
    29→
    30→# Map our relation_operator to FHIR comparator
    31→_COMPARATOR_MAP: dict[str, str] = {
    32→    ">": "gt",
    33→    ">=": "ge",
    34→    "<": "lt",
    35→    "<=": "le",
    36→    "gt": "gt",
    37→    "gte": "ge",
    38→    "lt": "lt",
    39→    "lte": "le",
    40→}
    41→
    42→
    43→def build_fhir_group_export(data: ProtocolExportData) -> dict[str, Any]:
    44→    """Build a FHIR R4 Group resource from structured criteria.
    45→
    46→    Args:
    47→        data: Loaded protocol export data.
    48→
    49→    Returns:
    50→        Dict representing the FHIR Group resource.
    51→    """
    52→    characteristics: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    53→
    54→    for criterion in data.criteria:
    55→        tree = criterion.structured_criterion
    56→        if not tree:
    57→            continue
    58→
    59→        is_exclusion = criterion.criteria_type == "exclusion"
    60→        chars = _build_characteristics_from_tree(tree, data, exclude=is_exclusion)
    61→        characteristics.extend(chars)
    62→
    63→    group: dict[str, Any] = {
    64→        "resourceType": "Group",
    65→        "id": data.protocol.id,
    66→        "type": "person",
    67→        "actual": False,
    68→        "name": data.protocol.title,
    69→        "characteristic": characteristics,
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    # Set combination method if we have characteristics
    73→    if characteristics:
    74→        group["extension"] = [
    75→            {
    76→                "url": (
    77→                    "http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/ebm/StructureDefinition"
    78→                    "/characteristic-combination"
    79→                ),
    80→                "valueCode": "all-of",
    81→            }
    82→        ]
    83→
    84→    return group
    85→
    86→
    87→def _build_or_characteristic(
    88→    tree: dict[str, Any],
    89→    data: ProtocolExportData,
    90→    exclude: bool,
    91→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    92→    """Build a nested FHIR Group for OR logic."""
    93→    children = tree.get("children", [])
    94→    or_chars: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    95→    for child in children:
    96→        or_chars.extend(_build_characteristics_from_tree(child, data, exclude=exclude))
    97→    if not or_chars:
    98→        return []
    99→
   100→    nested_group_id = str(uuid4())
   101→    nested_group: dict[str, Any] = {
   102→        "resourceType": "Group",
   103→        "id": nested_group_id,
   104→        "type": "person",
   105→        "actual": False,
   106→        "characteristic": or_chars,
   107→        "extension": [
   108→            {
   109→                "url": (
   110→                    "http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/ebm/StructureDefinition"
   111→                    "/characteristic-combination"
   112→                ),
   113→                "valueCode": "any-of",
   114→            }
   115→        ],
   116→    }
   117→    return [
   118→        {
   119→            "code": {"text": "Nested OR group"},
   120→            "valueReference": {"reference": f"#/{nested_group_id}"},
   121→            "exclude": exclude,
   122→            "_contained": nested_group,
   123→        }
   124→    ]
   125→
   126→
   127→def _build_characteristics_from_tree(
   128→    tree: dict[str, Any],
   129→    data: ProtocolExportData,
   130→    exclude: bool = False,
   131→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   132→    """Recursively build FHIR characteristics from an expression tree."""
   133→    node_type = tree.get("type", "").upper()
   134→
   135→    if node_type == "ATOMIC":
   136→        atomic_id = tree.get("atomic_criterion_id")
   137→        atomic = data.atomics_by_id.get(atomic_id) if atomic_id else None
   138→        if not atomic:
   139→            return []
   140→        char = _build_characteristic(atomic, exclude=exclude)
   141→        return [char] if char else []
   142→
   143→    if node_type == "AND":
   144→        result: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   145→        for child in tree.get("children", []):
   146→            result.extend(
   147→                _build_characteristics_from_tree(child, data, exclude=exclude)
   148→            )
   149→        return result
   150→
   151→    if node_type == "OR":
   152→        return _build_or_characteristic(tree, data, exclude)
   153→
   154→    if node_type == "NOT":
   155→        children = tree.get("children", [])
   156→        if not children:
   157→            return []
   158→        return _build_characteristics_from_tree(children[0], data, exclude=not exclude)
   159→
   160→    return []
   161→
   162→
   163→def _get_system_uri(system: str | None) -> str:
   164→    """Map an entity_concept_system to a FHIR system URI."""
   165→    if not system:
   166→        return "http://ohdsi.org/omop/concept"
   167→    return _SYSTEM_URI_MAP.get(system.lower(), f"urn:oid:{system}")
   168→
   169→
   170→def _get_concept_code(atomic: AtomicCriterion) -> str | None:
   171→    """Get the best concept code for an atomic criterion.
   172→
   173→    Delegates to the shared get_concept_code() helper.
   174→    """
   175→    return get_concept_code(atomic)
   176→
   177→
   178→def _build_demographic_characteristic(
   179→    atomic: AtomicCriterion,
   180→    exclude: bool = False,
   181→) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   182→    """Build a FHIR characteristic for demographics (age).
   183→
   184→    Uses the usage-context-type CodeSystem for age instead of
   185→    a SNOMED coded concept. The matcher derives age from birthDate.
   186→    """
   187→    if atomic.value_numeric is None:
   188→        return None
   189→
   190→    quantity: dict[str, Any] = {
   191→        "value": atomic.value_numeric,
   192→        "unit": atomic.unit_text or "years",
   193→        "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org",
   194→        "code": "a",
   195→    }
   196→    if atomic.relation_operator:
   197→        comparator = _COMPARATOR_MAP.get(atomic.relation_operator)
   198→        if comparator:
   199→            quantity["comparator"] = comparator
   200→
   201→    return {
   202→        "code": {
   203→            "coding": [
   204→                {
   205→                    "system": (
   206→                        "http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/usage-context-type"
   207→                    ),
   208→                    "code": "age",
   209→                    "display": "Age Range",
   210→                }
   211→            ],
   212→        },
   213→        "exclude": exclude,
   214→        "valueQuantity": quantity,
   215→    }
   216→
   217→
   218→def _build_characteristic(
   219→    atomic: AtomicCriterion,
   220→    exclude: bool = False,
   221→) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   222→    """Build a single FHIR Group characteristic from an AtomicCriterion."""
   223→    # Demographics: use age context type (not a coded concept)
   224→    if (atomic.entity_domain or "").lower() == "demographics":
   225→        return _build_demographic_characteristic(atomic, exclude=exclude)
   226→
   227→    concept_code = _get_concept_code(atomic)
   228→    if concept_code is None:
   229→        return None
   230→
   231→    system_uri = _get_system_uri(atomic.entity_concept_system)
   232→
   233→    char: dict[str, Any] = {
   234→        "code": {
   235→            "coding": [
   236→                {
   237→                    "system": system_uri,
   238→                    "code": concept_code,
   239→                    "display": atomic.original_text or "",
   240→                }
   241→            ],
   242→        },
   243→        "exclude": exclude or atomic.negation,
   244→    }
   245→
   246→    # Add value: quantity or text
   247→    if atomic.value_numeric is not None:
   248→        quantity: dict[str, Any] = {
   249→            "value": atomic.value_numeric,
   250→        }
   251→        if atomic.unit_text:
   252→            quantity["unit"] = atomic.unit_text
   253→        if atomic.relation_operator:
   254→            comparator = _COMPARATOR_MAP.get(atomic.relation_operator)
   255→            if comparator:
   256→                quantity["comparator"] = comparator
   257→        char["valueQuantity"] = quantity
   258→    elif atomic.value_text:
   259→        char["valueCodeableConcept"] = {
   260→            "text": atomic.value_text,
   261→        }
   262→    else:
   263→        # Boolean presence/absence
   264→        char["valueBoolean"] = not atomic.negation
   265→
   266→    return char
   267→

1→"""OMOP CDM v5.4 evaluation SQL generator.
     2→
     3→Generates ready-to-run SQL that evaluates a protocol's eligibility criteria
     4→against an OMOP CDM database. The SQL is returned as text, not executed.
     5→
     6→Limitation: This builder uses a flat AND/OR model. All inclusion atomics are
     7→combined with AND (all required); all exclusion atomics use NOT EXISTS (any
     8→disqualifies). The expression tree's nested AND/OR/NOT structure is NOT
     9→respected. For example, "HbA1c >= 7% OR fasting glucose >= 126" is evaluated
    10→as requiring both rather than either. The CIRCE and FHIR Group builders
    11→correctly walk the expression tree. A future enhancement could add tree-aware
    12→SQL generation using recursive CTE grouping.
    13→"""
    14→
    15→from __future__ import annotations
    16→
    17→from shared.models import AtomicCriterion
    18→
    19→from api_service.exporters import ProtocolExportData
    20→from api_service.exporters.concept_utils import get_concept_id
    21→
    22→# Map entity_domain to OMOP CDM table + concept_id column
    23→_DOMAIN_TABLE: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
    24→    "condition": ("condition_occurrence", "condition_concept_id"),
    25→    "measurement": ("measurement", "measurement_concept_id"),
    26→    "drug": ("drug_exposure", "drug_concept_id"),
    27→    "procedure": ("procedure_occurrence", "procedure_concept_id"),
    28→    "observation": ("observation", "observation_concept_id"),
    29→    "device": ("device_exposure", "device_concept_id"),
    30→    "visit": ("visit_occurrence", "visit_concept_id"),
    31→}
    32→
    33→# Map relation_operator to SQL operator
    34→_SQL_OP: dict[str, str] = {
    35→    ">": ">",
    36→    ">=": ">=",
    37→    "<": "<",
    38→    "<=": "<=",
    39→    "=": "=",
    40→    "==": "=",
    41→    "!=": "!=",
    42→    "gt": ">",
    43→    "gte": ">=",
    44→    "lt": "<",
    45→    "lte": "<=",
    46→    "eq": "=",
    47→    "neq": "!=",
    48→}
    49→
    50→
    51→def build_evaluation_sql(data: ProtocolExportData) -> str:
    52→    """Generate OMOP CDM evaluation SQL from structured criteria.
    53→
    54→    Produces:
    55→    1. Per-atomic CTEs using concept_ancestor for descendant expansion
    56→    2. Domain-specific evaluation logic
    57→    3. Final eligibility query combining inclusion/exclusion
    58→
    59→    Args:
    60→        data: Loaded protocol export data.
    61→
    62→    Returns:
    63→        SQL string ready for execution against an OMOP CDM v5.4 database.
    64→    """
    65→    ctes: list[str] = []
    66→    inclusion_cte_names: list[str] = []
    67→    exclusion_cte_names: list[str] = []
    68→
    69→    for i, atomic in enumerate(data.atomics):
    70→        concept_id = _get_valid_concept_id(atomic)
    71→        if concept_id is None:
    72→            continue
    73→
    74→        cte_name = f"cte_{i}"
    75→        cte_sql = _build_atomic_cte(atomic, concept_id, cte_name)
    76→        ctes.append(cte_sql)
    77→
    78→        if atomic.inclusion_exclusion == "exclusion" or atomic.negation:
    79→            exclusion_cte_names.append(cte_name)
    80→        else:
    81→            inclusion_cte_names.append(cte_name)
    82→
    83→    if not ctes:
    84→        return (
    85→            "-- No structured criteria with valid concept IDs found.\n"
    86→            "SELECT NULL AS person_id WHERE 1=0;\n"
    87→        )
    88→
    89→    parts: list[str] = []
    90→    parts.append("-- Auto-generated OMOP CDM v5.4 eligibility evaluation SQL")
    91→    parts.append(
    92→        "-- WARNING: This SQL uses flat AND/OR semantics. All inclusion criteria\n"
    93→        "-- are combined with AND (all required); exclusion criteria use NOT EXISTS.\n"
    94→        "-- Nested AND/OR/NOT structure from the expression tree is NOT respected.\n"
    95→        "-- Use the CIRCE or FHIR Group export for tree-aware logic."
    96→    )
    97→    parts.append(f"-- Protocol: {data.protocol.title} ({data.protocol.id})")
    98→    parts.append(f"-- Generated from {len(ctes)} atomic criteria\n")
    99→    parts.append("WITH")
   100→    parts.append(",\n\n".join(ctes))
   101→
   102→    # Build final SELECT
   103→    parts.append("\n\nSELECT p.person_id")
   104→    parts.append("FROM person p")
   105→
   106→    # Inclusion: require all
   107→    for cte_name in inclusion_cte_names:
   108→        parts.append(
   109→            f"WHERE EXISTS (\n"
   110→            f"    SELECT 1 FROM {cte_name} c\n"
   111→            f"    WHERE c.person_id = p.person_id\n"
   112→            f")"
   113→            if cte_name == inclusion_cte_names[0]
   114→            else f"AND EXISTS (\n"
   115→            f"    SELECT 1 FROM {cte_name} c\n"
   116→            f"    WHERE c.person_id = p.person_id\n"
   117→            f")"
   118→        )
   119→
   120→    # Exclusion: reject any
   121→    for cte_name in exclusion_cte_names:
   122→        prefix = (
   123→            "AND"
   124→            if inclusion_cte_names
   125→            else ("WHERE" if cte_name == exclusion_cte_names[0] else "AND")
   126→        )
   127→        parts.append(
   128→            f"{prefix} NOT EXISTS (\n"
   129→            f"    SELECT 1 FROM {cte_name} c\n"
   130→            f"    WHERE c.person_id = p.person_id\n"
   131→            f")"
   132→        )
   133→
   134→    parts.append(";")
   135→    return "\n".join(parts)
   136→
   137→
   138→def _get_valid_concept_id(atomic: AtomicCriterion) -> int | None:
   139→    """Get a validated integer concept ID for SQL interpolation.
   140→
   141→    Delegates to the shared get_concept_id() helper.
   142→    """
   143→    return get_concept_id(atomic)
   144→
   145→
   146→def _build_atomic_cte(atomic: AtomicCriterion, concept_id: int, cte_name: str) -> str:
   147→    """Build a CTE for a single atomic criterion."""
   148→    domain = (atomic.entity_domain or "condition").lower()
   149→
   150→    # Demographics: special handling for age
   151→    if domain == "demographics":
   152→        return _build_demographics_cte(atomic, cte_name)
   153→
   154→    table_name, concept_col = _DOMAIN_TABLE.get(
   155→        domain, ("condition_occurrence", "condition_concept_id")
   156→    )
   157→
   158→    lines: list[str] = []
   159→    lines.append(f"{cte_name} AS (")
   160→    lines.append("    SELECT DISTINCT t.person_id")
   161→    lines.append(f"    FROM {table_name} t")
   162→    lines.append("    INNER JOIN concept_ancestor ca")
   163→    lines.append(f"        ON ca.descendant_concept_id = t.{concept_col}")
   164→    lines.append(f"    WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = {concept_id}")
   165→
   166→    # Measurement value filter
   167→    is_measurement = (
   168→        domain == "measurement"
   169→        and atomic.relation_operator
   170→        and atomic.value_numeric is not None
   171→    )
   172→    if is_measurement and atomic.value_numeric is not None:
   173→        sql_op = _SQL_OP.get(atomic.relation_operator or "=", "=")
   174→        val = float(atomic.value_numeric)
   175→        lines.append(f"    AND t.value_as_number {sql_op} {val}")
   176→        if atomic.unit_concept_id is not None:
   177→            unit_id = int(atomic.unit_concept_id)
   178→            lines.append(f"    AND t.unit_concept_id = {unit_id}")
   179→
   180→    lines.append(")")
   181→    return "\n".join(lines)
   182→
   183→
   184→def _build_demographics_cte(atomic: AtomicCriterion, cte_name: str) -> str:
   185→    """Build a CTE for demographics-based criteria (age)."""
   186→    lines: list[str] = []
   187→    lines.append(f"{cte_name} AS (")
   188→    lines.append("    SELECT p.person_id")
   189→    lines.append("    FROM person p")
   190→
   191→    if atomic.relation_operator and atomic.value_numeric is not None:
   192→        sql_op = _SQL_OP.get(atomic.relation_operator or "=", "=")
   193→        lines.append(
   194→            f"    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - p.year_of_birth"
   195→            f" {sql_op} {int(atomic.value_numeric)}"
   196→        )
   197→    else:
   198→        lines.append("    WHERE 1=1")
   199→
   200→    lines.append(")")
   201→    return "\n".join(lines)
   202→

Design a plan for separating value from unit in the grounding golden test fixtures and linking units to medical terminology codes (UCUM, OMOP, and optionally UMLS/SNOMED).

## Context

The project is a clinical trial protocol analysis pipeline. The file `tests/e2e/test_snippets.json` contains golden examples for grounding validation. Currently, each grounding entity looks like:

```json
{
  "entity_name": "Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate",
  "system": "UMLS",
  "code": "C0858118",
  "relation": "<",
  "value": "45 ml/min"  // <-- unit embedded in value string
}
```

The user wants to:
1. Separate the numeric value from the unit in the golden examples
2. Link each unit to terminology codes (primarily UCUM + OMOP concept_id)
3. Plan the downstream impact across the rest of the app

## What Already Exists

### Backend (already separates value/unit):
- **`FieldMappingValue`** (`field_mapper.py:47-80`): Already has `type` discriminator with `value`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `duration` fields
- **`FieldMappingItem`** (`field_mapper.py:88-122`): Has `value: FieldMappingValue` + `unit: str` + `value_concept_id` + `value_concept_system`
- **`AtomicCriterion`** (`shared/models.py:184-233`): Already has:
  - `value_numeric: float | None`
  - `value_text: str | None` 
  - `unit_text: str | None`
  - `unit_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP via UCUM)
  - `value_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP for categoricals)

### Unit Normalization (already links to OMOP):
- **`normalize_unit()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:78-94`): Returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`
  - Known mappings: "%" → (%, 8554), "mg/dL" → (mg/dL, 8840), "years" → (a, 9448), "mL/min" → (mL/min, 8795), "kg/m2" → (kg/m2, 9531), "mL/min/1.73m2" → (mL/min/1.73m2, 720870), "{score}" → ({score}, 8527)
- **`normalize_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:118-136`): Categorical value lookup ("positive" → 45884084, "negative" → 45878583)
- **`normalize_ordinal_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:169-215`): Ordinal scale lookup, always returns unit_concept_id=8527 ({score})

### Exporters (already use unit_concept_id):
- **CIRCE exporter** (`circe_builder.py:200-214`): Exports `UnitConceptId` in ValueAsNumber filter
- **Evaluation SQL** (`evaluation_sql_builder.py:172-178`): Filters on `unit_concept_id`
- **FHIR exporter** (`fhir_group_builder.py:178-200`): Uses unit_text + UCUM system URI

### Frontend (already displays separate value/unit):
- **`FieldValue`** (`types.ts:19-38`): TypeScript discriminated union with StandardValue{value, unit}, RangeValue{min, max, unit}, TemporalValue{duration, unit}
- **`FieldMapping`** (`types.ts:41-48`): Has entity_code, entity_system, omop_concept_id
- **`ValueInput.tsx`**: Separate input fields for value and unit
- **`FieldMappingBadges.tsx`**: Displays formatted value + unit

### Database:
- **AtomicCriterion** already has `unit_text` (str) and `unit_concept_id` (int, OMOP)
- Does NOT have: `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_vocabulary_id`, or multi-terminology unit fields

### Test Infrastructure:
- **`test_grounding_snippets.py`**: 68 tests validating entity_name, code, relation, value, entity counts
- Currently no assertions on unit fields at all

## The 9 Grounding Snippets — Proposed Value/Unit Decomposition

Snippet 0: "Serum creatinine >1.5 times ULN"
- value: "1.5", unit: "times ULN", ucum: null, omop: null (no standard code for relative units)

Snippet 1: "eGFR <45 ml/min"
- value: "45", unit: "mL/min", ucum: "mL/min", omop: 8795

Snippet 2: "Body weight <50 kg" + "BMI >44 kg/m2"
- weight: value "50", unit: "kg", ucum: "kg", omop: 8576
- BMI: value "44", unit: "kg/m2", ucum: "kg/m2", omop: 9531

Snippets 3,4,6,7,8: Boolean presence/absence (True/True != etc.)
- value: "True", unit: null, ucum: null, omop: null

Snippet 5: "ASA physical status 1, 2, or 3"
- value: "1, 2, or 3", unit: "{score}", ucum: "{score}", omop: 8527

## Design Requirements

1. **test_snippets.json** — Define exact new schema for each entity
2. **test_grounding_snippets.py** — New assertions for unit fields
3. **AtomicCriterion model** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code` column (currently only has `unit_concept_id`)
4. **unit_normalizer.py** — Consider returning UCUM code alongside OMOP ID (it already does — `normalize_unit()` returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`)
5. **structure_builder.py** — Store UCUM code in a new AtomicCriterion column
6. **Frontend FieldMapping type** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_omop_concept_id` fields
7. **evaluate_prompt_changes.py** — Validate unit fields
8. **Exporters** — FHIR exporter could use the UCUM code directly instead of hardcoded "a"

## Key Design Question
The `normalize_unit()` function already returns both `ucum_code` and `omop_concept_id`. The `_create_atomic_from_mapping()` function in structure_builder.py currently only stores `unit_concept_id` (the OMOP ID). The UCUM code is discarded. We should persist the UCUM code too.

For UMLS/SNOMED unit codes: UCUM is the gold standard for units in both OMOP and FHIR. UMLS CUIs for units exist but are rarely used in clinical informatics. SNOMED has some unit concepts. The pragmatic approach is UCUM + OMOP, with an optional SNOMED fallback note.

Provide a detailed, phased plan covering all layers.

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""Evaluate prompt optimization changes against test_snippets.json.
     3→
     4→Renders each template with actual test snippet data, compares old (git HEAD~1)
     5→vs new (working tree) token counts, and validates template rendering.
     6→
     7→Usage:
     8→    uv run python scripts/evaluate_prompt_changes.py
     9→"""
    10→
    11→from __future__ import annotations
    12→
    13→import json
    14→import subprocess
    15→import sys
    16→from pathlib import Path
    17→
    18→from jinja2 import Environment, BaseLoader, TemplateSyntaxError
    19→
    20→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21→# Paths
    22→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    23→PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    24→PROMPTS_DIR = (
    25→    PROJECT_ROOT
    26→    / "services"
    27→    / "protocol-processor-service"
    28→    / "src"
    29→    / "protocol_processor"
    30→    / "prompts"
    31→)
    32→SNIPPETS_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "tests" / "e2e" / "test_snippets.json"
    33→
    34→JINJA_ENV = Environment(loader=BaseLoader(), undefined=__import__("jinja2").Undefined)
    35→
    36→# Templates and the git-relative paths used for `git show`
    37→TEMPLATE_FILES = {
    38→    "grounding_system.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/grounding_system.jinja2",
    39→    "grounding_evaluate.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/grounding_evaluate.jinja2",
    40→    "grounding_reasoning.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/grounding_reasoning.jinja2",
    41→    "entity_decompose.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/entity_decompose.jinja2",
    42→    "system.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/system.jinja2",
    43→    "user.jinja2": "services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/prompts/user.jinja2",
    44→}
    45→
    46→
    47→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48→# Helpers
    49→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    50→def tok(text: str) -> int:
    51→    """Approximate token count (words * 1.3)."""
    52→    return int(len(text.split()) * 1.3)
    53→
    54→
    55→def load_snippets() -> dict:
    56→    if not SNIPPETS_PATH.exists():
    57→        print(f"ERROR: {SNIPPETS_PATH} not found")
    58→        sys.exit(1)
    59→    return json.loads(SNIPPETS_PATH.read_text())
    60→
    61→
    62→def git_show(git_path: str, ref: str = "HEAD~1") -> str | None:
    63→    """Return file contents at a git ref, or None if unavailable."""
    64→    try:
    65→        result = subprocess.run(
    66→            ["git", "show", f"{ref}:{git_path}"],
    67→            capture_output=True,
    68→            text=True,
    69→            cwd=PROJECT_ROOT,
    70→        )
    71→        if result.returncode == 0:
    72→            return result.stdout
    73→    except Exception:
    74→        pass
    75→    return None
    76→
    77→
    78→def render(template_str: str, ctx: dict) -> str:
    79→    """Render a Jinja2 template string with the given context."""
    80→    try:
    81→        tmpl = JINJA_ENV.from_string(template_str)
    82→        return tmpl.render(**ctx)
    83→    except TemplateSyntaxError as exc:
    84→        return f"[RENDER ERROR: {exc}]"
    85→
    86→
    87→def make_candidate(entity: dict) -> dict:
    88→    """Build a fake candidate dict that mirrors real API shape."""
    89→    return {
    90→        "source_api": entity.get("system", "UMLS"),
    91→        "code": entity.get("code", "C0000000"),
    92→        "preferred_term": entity.get("entity_name", ""),
    93→        "semantic_type": "Clinical Finding",
    94→        "score": 0.95,
    95→    }
    96→
    97→
    98→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    99→# Evaluation runners
   100→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   101→def evaluate_entity_decompose(
   102→    snippets: dict, old_src: str | None, new_src: str
   103→) -> list[dict]:
   104→    """Render entity_decompose for each extraction snippet."""
   105→    rows = []
   106→    for i, snip in enumerate(snippets["extraction_test_snippets"]):
   107→        ctx = {"criterion_text": snip["snippet_text"], "category": None}
   108→        new_rendered = render(new_src, ctx)
   109→        old_rendered = render(old_src, ctx) if old_src else ""
   110→        rows.append(
   111→            {
   112→                "snippet_idx": i,
   113→                "input": snip["snippet_text"][:80],
   114→                "expected_class": snip["classification"],
   115→                "old_tokens": tok(old_rendered) if old_src else "N/A",
   116→                "new_tokens": tok(new_rendered),
   117→                "renders_ok": "[RENDER ERROR" not in new_rendered,
   118→            }
   119→        )

   122→
   123→def evaluate_grounding_chain(
   124→    snippets: dict,
   125→    old_sys: str | None,
   126→    new_sys: str,
   127→    old_eval: str | None,
   128→    new_eval: str,
   129→    old_reason: str | None,
   130→    new_reason: str,
   131→) -> list[dict]:
   132→    """Render grounding chain for each grounding snippet."""
   133→    rows = []
   134→    for i, snip in enumerate(snippets["grounding_test_snippets"]):
   135→        for ent in snip["entities"]:
   136→            # -- system prompt (static) --
   137→            sys_new_tok = tok(new_sys)
   138→            sys_old_tok = tok(old_sys) if old_sys else sys_new_tok
   139→
   140→            # -- evaluate prompt --
   141→            eval_ctx = {
   142→                "entity_text": ent["entity_name"],
   143→                "entity_type": "Condition",  # most common
   144→                "criterion_context": snip["snippet_text"],
   145→                "candidates": [make_candidate(ent)],
   146→            }
   147→            eval_new = render(new_eval, eval_ctx)
   148→            eval_old = render(old_eval, eval_ctx) if old_eval else ""
   149→
   150→            # -- reasoning prompt --
   151→            reason_ctx = {
   152→                "entity_text": ent["entity_name"],
   153→                "entity_type": "Condition",
   154→                "criterion_context": snip["snippet_text"],
   155→                "previous_query": None,
   156→                "attempt": 1,
   157→            }
   158→            reason_new = render(new_reason, reason_ctx)
   159→            reason_old = render(old_reason, reason_ctx) if old_reason else ""
   160→
   161→            total_old = sys_old_tok + tok(eval_old) + tok(reason_old) if old_sys else 0
   162→            total_new = sys_new_tok + tok(eval_new) + tok(reason_new)
   163→
   164→            rows.append(
   165→                {
   166→                    "snippet_idx": i,
   167→                    "entity": ent["entity_name"][:40],
   168→                    "code": ent["code"],
   169→                    "relation": ent["relation"],
   170→                    "old_chain_tokens": total_old if total_old else "N/A",
   171→                    "new_chain_tokens": total_new,

Design a plan for separating value from unit in the grounding golden test fixtures and linking units to medical terminology codes (UCUM, OMOP, and optionally UMLS/SNOMED).

## Context

The project is a clinical trial protocol analysis pipeline. The file `tests/e2e/test_snippets.json` contains golden examples for grounding validation. Currently, each grounding entity looks like:

```json
{
  "entity_name": "Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate",
  "system": "UMLS",
  "code": "C0858118",
  "relation": "<",
  "value": "45 ml/min"  // <-- unit embedded in value string
}
```

The user wants to:
1. Separate the numeric value from the unit in the golden examples
2. Link each unit to terminology codes (primarily UCUM + OMOP concept_id)
3. Plan the downstream impact across the rest of the app

## What Already Exists

### Backend (already separates value/unit):
- **`FieldMappingValue`** (`field_mapper.py:47-80`): Already has `type` discriminator with `value`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `duration` fields
- **`FieldMappingItem`** (`field_mapper.py:88-122`): Has `value: FieldMappingValue` + `unit: str` + `value_concept_id` + `value_concept_system`
- **`AtomicCriterion`** (`shared/models.py:184-233`): Already has:
  - `value_numeric: float | None`
  - `value_text: str | None` 
  - `unit_text: str | None`
  - `unit_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP via UCUM)
  - `value_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP for categoricals)

### Unit Normalization (already links to OMOP):
- **`normalize_unit()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:78-94`): Returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`
  - Known mappings: "%" → (%, 8554), "mg/dL" → (mg/dL, 8840), "years" → (a, 9448), "mL/min" → (mL/min, 8795), "kg/m2" → (kg/m2, 9531), "mL/min/1.73m2" → (mL/min/1.73m2, 720870), "{score}" → ({score}, 8527)
- **`normalize_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:118-136`): Categorical value lookup ("positive" → 45884084, "negative" → 45878583)
- **`normalize_ordinal_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:169-215`): Ordinal scale lookup, always returns unit_concept_id=8527 ({score})

### Exporters (already use unit_concept_id):
- **CIRCE exporter** (`circe_builder.py:200-214`): Exports `UnitConceptId` in ValueAsNumber filter
- **Evaluation SQL** (`evaluation_sql_builder.py:172-178`): Filters on `unit_concept_id`
- **FHIR exporter** (`fhir_group_builder.py:178-200`): Uses unit_text + UCUM system URI

### Frontend (already displays separate value/unit):
- **`FieldValue`** (`types.ts:19-38`): TypeScript discriminated union with StandardValue{value, unit}, RangeValue{min, max, unit}, TemporalValue{duration, unit}
- **`FieldMapping`** (`types.ts:41-48`): Has entity_code, entity_system, omop_concept_id
- **`ValueInput.tsx`**: Separate input fields for value and unit
- **`FieldMappingBadges.tsx`**: Displays formatted value + unit

### Database:
- **AtomicCriterion** already has `unit_text` (str) and `unit_concept_id` (int, OMOP)
- Does NOT have: `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_vocabulary_id`, or multi-terminology unit fields

### Test Infrastructure:
- **`test_grounding_snippets.py`**: 68 tests validating entity_name, code, relation, value, entity counts
- Currently no assertions on unit fields at all

## The 9 Grounding Snippets — Proposed Value/Unit Decomposition

Snippet 0: "Serum creatinine >1.5 times ULN"
- value: "1.5", unit: "times ULN", ucum: null, omop: null (no standard code for relative units)

Snippet 1: "eGFR <45 ml/min"
- value: "45", unit: "mL/min", ucum: "mL/min", omop: 8795

Snippet 2: "Body weight <50 kg" + "BMI >44 kg/m2"
- weight: value "50", unit: "kg", ucum: "kg", omop: 8576
- BMI: value "44", unit: "kg/m2", ucum: "kg/m2", omop: 9531

Snippets 3,4,6,7,8: Boolean presence/absence (True/True != etc.)
- value: "True", unit: null, ucum: null, omop: null

Snippet 5: "ASA physical status 1, 2, or 3"
- value: "1, 2, or 3", unit: "{score}", ucum: "{score}", omop: 8527

## Design Requirements

1. **test_snippets.json** — Define exact new schema for each entity
2. **test_grounding_snippets.py** — New assertions for unit fields
3. **AtomicCriterion model** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code` column (currently only has `unit_concept_id`)
4. **unit_normalizer.py** — Consider returning UCUM code alongside OMOP ID (it already does — `normalize_unit()` returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`)
5. **structure_builder.py** — Store UCUM code in a new AtomicCriterion column
6. **Frontend FieldMapping type** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_omop_concept_id` fields
7. **evaluate_prompt_changes.py** — Validate unit fields
8. **Exporters** — FHIR exporter could use the UCUM code directly instead of hardcoded "a"

## Key Design Question
The `normalize_unit()` function already returns both `ucum_code` and `omop_concept_id`. The `_create_atomic_from_mapping()` function in structure_builder.py currently only stores `unit_concept_id` (the OMOP ID). The UCUM code is discarded. We should persist the UCUM code too.

For UMLS/SNOMED unit codes: UCUM is the gold standard for units in both OMOP and FHIR. UMLS CUIs for units exist but are rarely used in clinical informatics. SNOMED has some unit concepts. The pragmatic approach is UCUM + OMOP, with an optional SNOMED fallback note.

Provide a detailed, phased plan covering all layers.

## Context

The project is a clinical trial protocol analysis pipeline. The file `tests/e2e/test_snippets.json` contains golden examples for grounding validation. Currently, each grounding entity looks like:

```json

  "code": "C0858118",
  "relation": "<",
```

The user wants to:

### Backend (already separates value/unit):
- **`FieldMappingValue`** (`field_mapper.py:47-80`): Already has `type` discriminator with `value`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `duration` fields
- **`FieldMappingItem`** (`field_mapper.py:88-122`): Has `value: FieldMappingValue` + `unit: str` + `value_concept_id` + `value_concept_system`
- **`AtomicCriterion`** (`shared/models.py:184-233`): Already has:
  - `value_numeric: float | None`
  - `value_text: str | None` 
  - `unit_text: str | None`
  - `unit_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP via UCUM)
  - `value_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP for categoricals)

### Unit Normalization (already links to OMOP):
- **`normalize_unit()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:78-94`): Returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`
  - Known mappings: "%" → (%, 8554), "mg/dL" → (mg/dL, 8840), "years" → (a, 9448), "mL/min" → (mL/min, 8795), "kg/m2" → (kg/m2, 9531), "mL/min/1.73m2" → (mL/min/1.73m2, 720870), "{score}" → ({score}, 8527)

- **`normalize_ordinal_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:169-215`): Ordinal scale lookup, always returns unit_concept_id=8527 ({score})

- **FHIR exporter** (`fhir_group_builder.py:178-200`): Uses unit_text + UCUM system URI

- **`FieldValue`** (`types.ts:19-38`): TypeScript discriminated union with StandardValue{value, unit}, RangeValue{min, max, unit}, TemporalValue{duration, unit}
- **`FieldMapping`** (`types.ts:41-48`): Has entity_code, entity_system, omop_concept_id

- **AtomicCriterion** already has `unit_text` (str) and `unit_concept_id` (int, OMOP)
- Does NOT have: `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_vocabulary_id`, or multi-terminology unit fields

4. **unit_normalizer.py** — Consider returning UCUM code alongside OMOP ID (it already does — `normalize_unit()` returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`)
5. **structure_builder.py** — Store UCUM code in a new AtomicCriterion column
6. **Frontend FieldMapping type** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_omop_concept_id` fields
7. **evaluate_prompt_changes.py** — Validate unit fields

The project is a clinical trial protocol analysis pipeline. The file `tests/e2e/test_snippets.json` contains golden examples for grounding validation. Currently, each grounding entity looks like:

```json
{
  "entity_name": "Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate",
  "system": "UMLS",
  "code": "C0858118",
  "relation": "<",
  "value": "45 ml/min"  // <-- unit embedded in value string
}
```

The user wants to:
1. Separate the numeric value from the unit in the golden examples
2. Link each unit to terminology codes (primarily UCUM + OMOP concept_id)
3. Plan the downstream impact across the rest of the app

## What Already Exists

### Backend (already separates value/unit):
- **`FieldMappingValue`** (`field_mapper.py:47-80`): Already has `type` discriminator with `value`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `duration` fields
- **`FieldMappingItem`** (`field_mapper.py:88-122`): Has `value: FieldMappingValue` + `unit: str` + `value_concept_id` + `value_concept_system`
- **`AtomicCriterion`** (`shared/models.py:184-233`): Already has:
  - `value_numeric: float | None`
  - `value_text: str | None` 
  - `unit_text: str | None`
  - `unit_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP via UCUM)
  - `value_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP for categoricals)

### Unit Normalization (already links to OMOP):
- **`normalize_unit()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:78-94`): Returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`
  - Known mappings: "%" → (%, 8554), "mg/dL" → (mg/dL, 8840), "years" → (a, 9448), "mL/min" → (mL/min, 8795), "kg/m2" → (kg/m2, 9531), "mL/min/1.73m2" → (mL/min/1.73m2, 720870), "{score}" → ({score}, 8527)
- **`normalize_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:118-136`): Categorical value lookup ("positive" → 45884084, "negative" → 45878583)
- **`normalize_ordinal_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:169-215`): Ordinal scale lookup, always returns unit_concept_id=8527 ({score})

### Exporters (already use unit_concept_id):
- **CIRCE exporter** (`circe_builder.py:200-214`): Exports `UnitConceptId` in ValueAsNumber filter
- **Evaluation SQL** (`evaluation_sql_builder.py:172-178`): Filters on `unit_concept_id`
- **FHIR exporter** (`fhir_group_builder.py:178-200`): Uses unit_text + UCUM system URI

### Frontend (already displays separate value/unit):
- **`FieldValue`** (`types.ts:19-38`): TypeScript discriminated union with StandardValue{value, unit}, RangeValue{min, max, unit}, TemporalValue{duration, unit}
- **`FieldMapping`** (`types.ts:41-48`): Has entity_code, entity_system, omop_concept_id
- **`ValueInput.tsx`**: Separate input fields for value and unit
- **`FieldMappingBadges.tsx`**: Displays formatted value + unit

### Database:
- **AtomicCriterion** already has `unit_text` (str) and `unit_concept_id` (int, OMOP)
- Does NOT have: `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_vocabulary_id`, or multi-terminology unit fields

### Test Infrastructure:
- **`test_grounding_snippets.py`**: 68 tests validating entity_name, code, relation, value, entity counts
- Currently no assertions on unit fields at all

## The 9 Grounding Snippets — Proposed Value/Unit Decomposition

Snippet 0: "Serum creatinine >1.5 times ULN"
- value: "1.5", unit: "times ULN", ucum: null, omop: null (no standard code for relative units)

Snippet 1: "eGFR <45 ml/min"
- value: "45", unit: "mL/min", ucum: "mL/min", omop: 8795

Snippet 2: "Body weight <50 kg" + "BMI >44 kg/m2"
- weight: value "50", unit: "kg", ucum: "kg", omop: 8576
- BMI: value "44", unit: "kg/m2", ucum: "kg/m2", omop: 9531

Snippets 3,4,6,7,8: Boolean presence/absence (True/True != etc.)
- value: "True", unit: null, ucum: null, omop: null

Snippet 5: "ASA physical status 1, 2, or 3"
- value: "1, 2, or 3", unit: "{score}", ucum: "{score}", omop: 8527

## Design Requirements

1. **test_snippets.json** — Define exact new schema for each entity
2. **test_grounding_snippets.py** — New assertions for unit fields
3. **AtomicCriterion model** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code` column (currently only has `unit_concept_id`)
4. **unit_normalizer.py** — Consider returning UCUM code alongside OMOP ID (it already does — `normalize_unit()` returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`)
5. **structure_builder.py** — Store UCUM code in a new AtomicCriterion column
6. **Frontend FieldMapping type** — Consider adding `unit_ucum_code`, `unit_omop_concept_id` fields
7. **evaluate_prompt_changes.py** — Validate unit fields
8. **Exporters** — FHIR exporter could use the UCUM code directly instead of hardcoded "a"

## Key Design Question
The `normalize_unit()` function already returns both `ucum_code` and `omop_concept_id`. The `_create_atomic_from_mapping()` function in structure_builder.py currently only stores `unit_concept_id` (the OMOP ID). The UCUM code is discarded. We should persist the UCUM code too.

For UMLS/SNOMED unit codes: UCUM is the gold standard for units in both OMOP and FHIR. UMLS CUIs for units exist but are rarely used in clinical informatics. SNOMED has some unit concepts. The pragmatic approach is UCUM + OMOP, with an optional SNOMED fallback note.

Provide a detailed, phased plan covering all layers.

1→"""OMOP vocabulary mapper: look up standard OMOP concept_ids for medical entities.
     2→
     3→Queries Athena vocabulary tables (concept, concept_synonym) in a dedicated
     4→OMOP vocabulary database. Requires OMOP_VOCAB_URL environment variable
     5→pointing to a Postgres instance with loaded Athena vocabulary data.
     6→
     7→This tool provides the OMOP grounding leg of the dual-grounding pipeline:
     8→- TerminologyRouter provides UMLS/SNOMED/RxNorm/ICD-10/LOINC/HPO codes
     9→- OmopMapper provides OMOP standard concept_ids for CIRCE export and CDM joins
    10→
    11→Connection: Uses a dedicated SQLAlchemy engine created from OMOP_VOCAB_URL.
    12→This is separate from the main app database (DATABASE_URL). If OMOP_VOCAB_URL
    13→is not set, lookup_omop_concept raises RuntimeError — callers must handle this
    14→explicitly rather than silently receiving empty results.
    15→
    16→All DB I/O is synchronous SQLAlchemy wrapped in run_in_executor for async
    17→compatibility.
    18→"""
    19→
    20→from __future__ import annotations
    21→
    22→import asyncio
    23→import logging
    24→import os
    25→from difflib import SequenceMatcher
    26→from typing import Any
    27→
    28→from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
    29→from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
    30→
    31→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    32→
    33→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    34→# Configuration
    35→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36→
    37→OMOP_MIN_MATCH_SCORE: float = 0.3
    38→"""Minimum fuzzy-match score to accept a candidate. Below this, return None."""
    39→
    40→OMOP_MAX_CANDIDATES: int = 50
    41→"""Maximum number of rows to fetch from each SQL query (LIMIT clause)."""
    42→
    43→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    44→# Dedicated OMOP vocabulary engine (lazy singleton)
    45→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    46→
    47→_omop_engine: Any = None
    48→
    49→
    50→def _get_omop_engine() -> Any:
    51→    """Return the OMOP vocabulary SQLAlchemy engine.
    52→
    53→    Creates a dedicated engine from OMOP_VOCAB_URL on first call.
    54→    Raises RuntimeError if the env var is not set — callers must
    55→    handle this rather than silently degrading.
    56→    """
    57→    global _omop_engine  # noqa: PLW0603
    58→    if _omop_engine is not None:
    59→        return _omop_engine
    60→
    61→    omop_url = os.getenv("OMOP_VOCAB_URL")
    62→    if not omop_url:
    63→        raise RuntimeError(
    64→            "OMOP_VOCAB_URL environment variable is not set. "
    65→            "Set it to the OMOP vocabulary Postgres connection string "
    66→            "(e.g. postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5433/omop_vocab) "
    67→            "or start the omop-vocab container: "
    68→            "docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml --profile omop up -d"
    69→        )
    70→
    71→    _omop_engine = create_engine(omop_url, pool_pre_ping=True)
    72→    logger.info("OMOP vocabulary engine created: %s", omop_url.split("@")[-1])
    73→    return _omop_engine
    74→
    75→
    76→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    77→# Entity type -> OMOP domain mapping
    78→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    79→
    80→ENTITY_TYPE_TO_OMOP_DOMAIN: dict[str, str] = {
    81→    "Condition": "Condition",
    82→    "Medication": "Drug",
    83→    "Lab_Value": "Measurement",
    84→    "Procedure": "Procedure",
    85→    "Demographic": "Observation",
    86→}
    87→"""Map pipeline entity types to OMOP CDM domain_id values (legacy single-domain).
    88→
    89→Demographic is a catch-all routed to Observation. Entity types not present
    90→here will fall back to Observation as well.
    91→"""
    92→
    93→ENTITY_TYPE_TO_OMOP_DOMAINS: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    94→    "Condition": ["Condition", "Observation"],
    95→    "Medication": ["Drug"],
    96→    "Lab_Value": ["Measurement", "Observation"],
    97→    "Procedure": ["Procedure", "Observation"],
    98→    "Demographic": ["Observation", "Measurement"],
    99→}
   100→"""Map pipeline entity types to OMOP CDM domain_id values (multi-domain).
   101→
   102→Primary domain is first in the list. Fallback domains follow.
   103→Candidates from the primary domain receive a small scoring bonus.
   104→"""
   105→
   106→PRIMARY_DOMAIN_BONUS: float = 0.05
   107→"""Small scoring bonus applied to candidates from the primary (first) domain."""
   108→
   109→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   110→# Result schema
   111→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   112→
   113→
   114→class OmopLookupResult(BaseModel):
   115→    """Result of an OMOP vocabulary lookup for a single entity.
   116→
   117→    Attributes:
   118→        omop_concept_id: Matched OMOP concept_id as a string, or None.
   119→        omop_concept_name: Matched concept_name from the vocabulary, or None.
   120→        omop_vocabulary_id: Vocabulary source of the match (e.g. SNOMED, RxNorm).
   121→        omop_domain_id: OMOP domain_id of the matched concept.
   122→        match_score: Fuzzy similarity score between 0.0 and 1.0.
   123→        match_method: How the match was found: "concept_name" or "synonym".
   124→    """
   125→
   126→    omop_concept_id: str | None = Field(
   127→        default=None,
   128→        description=("Matched OMOP concept_id as a string, or None if no match."),
   129→    )
   130→    omop_concept_name: str | None = Field(
   131→        default=None,
   132→        description="Matched concept_name from the OMOP vocabulary.",
   133→    )
   134→    omop_vocabulary_id: str | None = Field(
   135→        default=None,
   136→        description=("Vocabulary source of the match (e.g. 'SNOMED', 'RxNorm')."),
   137→    )
   138→    omop_domain_id: str | None = Field(
   139→        default=None,
   140→        description="OMOP domain_id of the matched concept.",
   141→    )
   142→    match_score: float = Field(
   143→        default=0.0,
   144→        ge=0.0,
   145→        le=1.0,
   146→        description="Fuzzy similarity score between 0.0 and 1.0.",
   147→    )
   148→    match_method: str = Field(
   149→        default="",
   150→        description='How the match was found: "concept_name" or "synonym".',
   151→    )
   152→
   153→
   154→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   155→# Internal helpers
   156→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→
   158→
   159→def _score_candidates(
   160→    entity_text: str, candidates: list[dict[str, Any]]
   161→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   162→    """Score and sort candidates by fuzzy string similarity to *entity_text*.
   163→
   164→    Uses ``difflib.SequenceMatcher`` ratio as the base score, with a bonus
   165→    for exact case-insensitive substring containment.
   166→
   167→    Args:
   168→        entity_text: The original entity text to match against.
   169→        candidates: List of candidate dicts, each with at least a
   170→            ``"match_text"`` key containing the string to compare.
   171→
   172→    Returns:
   173→        The same candidate dicts augmented with a ``"score"`` key, sorted
   174→        in descending order of score.
   175→    """
   176→    entity_lower = entity_text.lower().strip()
   177→
   178→    for candidate in candidates:
   179→        match_text = candidate.get("match_text", "").lower().strip()
   180→
   181→        # Base score: SequenceMatcher ratio
   182→        base_score = SequenceMatcher(None, entity_lower, match_text).ratio()
   183→
   184→        # Bonus for exact substring containment (either direction)
   185→        bonus = 0.0
   186→        if entity_lower in match_text or match_text in entity_lower:
   187→            bonus = 0.15
   188→
   189→        # Bonus for exact match
   190→        if entity_lower == match_text:
   191→            bonus = 0.25
   192→
   193→        candidate["score"] = min(base_score + bonus, 1.0)
   194→
   195→    # Sort by score desc, then by length similarity (prefer match_text
   196→    # closest in length to entity_text) as tiebreaker.
   197→    entity_len = len(entity_lower)
   198→
   199→    def _sort_key(c: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[float, int]:
   200→        match_len = len(c.get("match_text", "").strip())
   201→        return (c["score"], -abs(match_len - entity_len))
   202→
   203→    candidates.sort(key=_sort_key, reverse=True)
   204→    return candidates
   205→
   206→
   207→def _get_domain_filter(entity_type: str) -> str:
   208→    """Resolve entity type to an OMOP domain_id filter value.
   209→
   210→    Falls back to ``"Observation"`` for unknown entity types.
   211→
   212→    Args:
   213→        entity_type: Pipeline entity type (e.g. "Condition", "Medication").
   214→
   215→    Returns:
   216→        OMOP domain_id string.
   217→    """
   218→    domain = ENTITY_TYPE_TO_OMOP_DOMAIN.get(entity_type, "Observation")
   219→    if entity_type not in ENTITY_TYPE_TO_OMOP_DOMAIN:
   220→        logger.info(
   221→            "Entity type '%s' not in OMOP domain map — defaulting to '%s'",
   222→            entity_type,
   223→            domain,
   224→        )
   225→    return domain
   226→
   227→
   228→def _get_domain_filters(entity_type: str) -> list[str]:
   229→    """Resolve entity type to a list of OMOP domain_id filter values.
   230→
   231→    Returns primary + fallback domains. The first domain in the list
   232→    is the primary domain (candidates from it receive a scoring bonus).
   233→    Falls back to ``["Observation"]`` for unknown entity types.
   234→
   235→    Args:
   236→        entity_type: Pipeline entity type (e.g. "Condition", "Medication").
   237→
   238→    Returns:
   239→        List of OMOP domain_id strings, primary first.
   240→    """
   241→    domains = ENTITY_TYPE_TO_OMOP_DOMAINS.get(entity_type)
   242→    if domains is not None:
   243→        return domains
   244→    logger.info(
   245→        "Entity type '%s' not in OMOP multi-domain map — defaulting to ['Observation']",
   246→        entity_type,
   247→    )
   248→    return ["Observation"]
   249→
   250→
   251→def _query_concept_table(
   252→    engine: Any, entity_text: str, domain_ids: list[str]
   253→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   254→    """Query concept table for standard concepts matching *entity_text*.
   255→
   256→    Args:
   257→        engine: SQLAlchemy engine for the OMOP vocabulary database.
   258→        entity_text: Text to search for (used in ILIKE pattern).
   259→        domain_ids: List of OMOP domain_id values to filter on.
   260→
   261→    Returns:
   262→        List of candidate dicts with keys: concept_id, concept_name,
   263→        domain_id, vocabulary_id, match_text, match_method.
   264→    """
   265→    # Build parameterized IN clause for domain_ids
   266→    domain_params = {f"d{i}": d for i, d in enumerate(domain_ids)}
   267→    domain_placeholders = ", ".join(f":d{i}" for i in range(len(domain_ids)))
   268→
   269→    sql = text(
   270→        "SELECT concept_id, concept_name, domain_id, vocabulary_id "
   271→        "FROM concept "
   272→        "WHERE standard_concept = 'S' "
   273→        f"  AND domain_id IN ({domain_placeholders}) "
   274→        "  AND concept_name ILIKE :pattern "
   275→        "ORDER BY length(concept_name) ASC "
   276→        "LIMIT :max_candidates"
   277→    )
   278→    pattern = f"%{entity_text}%"
   279→    params = {
   280→        **domain_params,
   281→        "pattern": pattern,
   282→        "max_candidates": OMOP_MAX_CANDIDATES,
   283→    }
   284→    with engine.connect() as conn:
   285→        rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
   286→
   287→    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   288→    for row in rows:
   289→        candidates.append(
   290→            {
   291→                "concept_id": str(row[0]),
   292→                "concept_name": row[1],
   293→                "domain_id": row[2],
   294→                "vocabulary_id": row[3],
   295→                "match_text": row[1],
   296→                "match_method": "concept_name",
   297→            }
   298→        )
   299→    return candidates
   300→
   301→
   302→def _query_synonym_table(
   303→    engine: Any,
   304→    entity_text: str,
   305→    domain_ids: list[str],
   306→    *,
   307→    skip_domain_filter: bool = False,
   308→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   309→    """Query concept_synonym joined with concept for synonym matches.
   310→
   311→    Args:
   312→        engine: SQLAlchemy engine for the OMOP vocabulary database.
   313→        entity_text: Text to search for (used in ILIKE pattern).
   314→        domain_ids: List of OMOP domain_id values to filter on.
   315→        skip_domain_filter: If True, search across ALL domains (used for
   316→            acronym lookups where the domain may be ambiguous).
   317→
   318→    Returns:
   319→        List of candidate dicts with keys: concept_id, concept_name,
   320→        domain_id, vocabulary_id, match_text, match_method.
   321→    """
   322→    pattern = f"%{entity_text}%"
   323→
   324→    if skip_domain_filter:
   325→        sql = text(
   326→            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, "
   327→            "       c.vocabulary_id, s.concept_synonym_name "
   328→            "FROM concept_synonym s "
   329→            "JOIN concept c ON s.concept_id = c.concept_id "
   330→            "WHERE c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   331→            "  AND s.concept_synonym_name ILIKE :pattern "
   332→            "ORDER BY length(s.concept_synonym_name) ASC "
   333→            "LIMIT :max_candidates"
   334→        )
   335→        params: dict[str, Any] = {
   336→            "pattern": pattern,
   337→            "max_candidates": OMOP_MAX_CANDIDATES,
   338→        }
   339→    else:
   340→        domain_params = {f"d{i}": d for i, d in enumerate(domain_ids)}
   341→        domain_placeholders = ", ".join(f":d{i}" for i in range(len(domain_ids)))
   342→        sql = text(
   343→            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.domain_id, "
   344→            "       c.vocabulary_id, s.concept_synonym_name "
   345→            "FROM concept_synonym s "
   346→            "JOIN concept c ON s.concept_id = c.concept_id "
   347→            "WHERE c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   348→            f"  AND c.domain_id IN ({domain_placeholders}) "
   349→            "  AND s.concept_synonym_name ILIKE :pattern "
   350→            "ORDER BY length(s.concept_synonym_name) ASC "
   351→            "LIMIT :max_candidates"
   352→        )
   353→        params = {
   354→            **domain_params,
   355→            "pattern": pattern,
   356→            "max_candidates": OMOP_MAX_CANDIDATES,
   357→        }
   358→
   359→    with engine.connect() as conn:
   360→        rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
   361→
   362→    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   363→    for row in rows:
   364→        candidates.append(
   365→            {
   366→                "concept_id": str(row[0]),
   367→                "concept_name": row[1],
   368→                "domain_id": row[2],
   369→                "vocabulary_id": row[3],
   370→                "match_text": row[4],  # synonym name used for scoring
   371→                "match_method": "synonym",
   372→            }
   373→        )
   374→    return candidates
   375→
   376→
   377→def _sync_lookup(
   378→    entity_text: str,
   379→    domain_ids: list[str],
   380→    *,
   381→    is_acronym: bool = False,
   382→) -> OmopLookupResult:
   383→    """Synchronous OMOP lookup — runs inside run_in_executor.
   384→
   385→    Queries both concept and concept_synonym tables, deduplicates
   386→    candidates by concept_id (preferring concept_name match), scores them,
   387→    and returns the best match above the threshold.
   388→
   389→    Args:
   390→        entity_text: The entity text to look up.
   391→        domain_ids: List of OMOP domain_id values to filter on.
   392→            The first domain is considered "primary" and gets a scoring bonus.
   393→        is_acronym: If True, skip domain filter for synonym search
   394→            (acronyms may appear in any OMOP domain).
   395→
   396→    Returns:
   397→        OmopLookupResult with best match, or empty result if nothing found
   398→        or all candidates score below OMOP_MIN_MATCH_SCORE.
   399→
   400→    Raises:
   401→        RuntimeError: If OMOP_VOCAB_URL is not configured.
   402→        Exception: Database errors are propagated, not swallowed.
   403→    """
   404→    engine = _get_omop_engine()
   405→
   406→    concept_candidates = _query_concept_table(engine, entity_text, domain_ids)
   407→    synonym_candidates = _query_synonym_table(
   408→        engine,
   409→        entity_text,
   410→        domain_ids,
   411→        skip_domain_filter=is_acronym,
   412→    )
   413→
   414→    # Deduplicate by concept_id — prefer concept_name match over synonym
   415→    seen: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   416→    for candidate in concept_candidates:
   417→        seen[candidate["concept_id"]] = candidate
   418→    for candidate in synonym_candidates:
   419→        if candidate["concept_id"] not in seen:
   420→            seen[candidate["concept_id"]] = candidate
   421→
   422→    all_candidates = list(seen.values())
   423→
   424→    if not all_candidates:
   425→        logger.debug(
   426→            "No OMOP candidates found for '%s' in domains %s",
   427→            entity_text[:50],
   428→            domain_ids,
   429→        )
   430→        return OmopLookupResult()
   431→
   432→    # Score and sort
   433→    scored = _score_candidates(entity_text, all_candidates)
   434→
   435→    # Apply primary domain bonus
   436→    primary_domain = domain_ids[0] if domain_ids else None
   437→    if primary_domain:
   438→        for candidate in scored:
   439→            if candidate.get("domain_id") == primary_domain:
   440→                candidate["score"] = min(candidate["score"] + PRIMARY_DOMAIN_BONUS, 1.0)
   441→        # Re-sort after bonus
   442→        scored.sort(key=lambda c: c["score"], reverse=True)
   443→
   444→    best = scored[0]
   445→
   446→    if best["score"] < OMOP_MIN_MATCH_SCORE:
   447→        logger.debug(
   448→            "Best OMOP candidate for '%s' scored %.3f "
   449→            "(below threshold %.2f) — skipping",
   450→            entity_text[:50],
   451→            best["score"],
   452→            OMOP_MIN_MATCH_SCORE,
   453→        )
   454→        return OmopLookupResult()
   455→
   456→    logger.info(
   457→        "OMOP match for '%s': concept_id=%s, name='%s', score=%.3f, method=%s",
   458→        entity_text[:50],
   459→        best["concept_id"],
   460→        best["concept_name"][:60],
   461→        best["score"],
   462→        best["match_method"],
   463→    )
   464→
   465→    return OmopLookupResult(
   466→        omop_concept_id=best["concept_id"],
   467→        omop_concept_name=best["concept_name"],
   468→        omop_vocabulary_id=best["vocabulary_id"],
   469→        omop_domain_id=best["domain_id"],
   470→        match_score=best["score"],
   471→        match_method=best["match_method"],
   472→    )
   473→
   474→
   475→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   476→# Public async API
   477→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   478→
   479→
   480→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   481→# Unit / value / ordinal DB lookups (used by unit_normalizer)
   482→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   483→
   484→
   485→def _lookup_ucum_unit(engine: Any, unit_text: str) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
   486→    """Query concept + concept_synonym where vocabulary_id='UCUM'.
   487→
   488→    Searches for *unit_text* (case-insensitive) in both concept_name and
   489→    concept_synonym_name within UCUM vocabulary. Returns the best match.
   490→
   491→    Args:
   492→        engine: SQLAlchemy engine for the OMOP vocabulary database.
   493→        unit_text: Raw unit string (e.g. "mg/dL", "years", "%").
   494→
   495→    Returns:
   496→        (ucum_code, omop_concept_id) or (None, None) if not found.
   497→    """
   498→    key = unit_text.strip()
   499→    if not key:
   500→        return (None, None)
   501→
   502→    # Try exact concept_name match first (fastest path)
   503→    sql_exact = text(
   504→        "SELECT concept_id, concept_name "
   505→        "FROM concept "
   506→        "WHERE vocabulary_id = 'UCUM' "
   507→        "  AND standard_concept = 'S' "
   508→        "  AND LOWER(concept_name) = LOWER(:unit_text) "
   509→        "LIMIT 1"
   510→    )
   511→    with engine.connect() as conn:
   512→        row = conn.execute(sql_exact, {"unit_text": key}).fetchone()
   513→        if row is not None:
   514→            return (row[1], int(row[0]))
   515→
   516→        # Try synonym match
   517→        sql_syn = text(
   518→            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name "
   519→            "FROM concept_synonym s "
   520→            "JOIN concept c ON s.concept_id = c.concept_id "
   521→            "WHERE c.vocabulary_id = 'UCUM' "
   522→            "  AND c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   523→            "  AND LOWER(s.concept_synonym_name) = LOWER(:unit_text) "
   524→            "LIMIT 1"
   525→        )
   526→        row = conn.execute(sql_syn, {"unit_text": key}).fetchone()
   527→        if row is not None:
   528→            return (row[1], int(row[0]))
   529→
   530→    return (None, None)
   531→
   532→
   533→def _lookup_value_concept(
   534→    engine: Any, value_text: str
   535→) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
   536→    """Query concept where domain_id='Meas Value' for SNOMED qualifiers.
   537→
   538→    Searches for categorical value terms like "positive", "negative",
   539→    "normal", "abnormal" in the Meas Value domain.
   540→
   541→    Args:
   542→        engine: SQLAlchemy engine for the OMOP vocabulary database.
   543→        value_text: Raw value text (e.g. "positive", "absent").
   544→
   545→    Returns:
   546→        (normalized_text, omop_concept_id) or (None, None) if not found.
   547→    """
   548→    key = value_text.strip()
   549→    if not key:
   550→        return (None, None)
   551→
   552→    sql = text(
   553→        "SELECT concept_id, concept_name "
   554→        "FROM concept "
   555→        "WHERE domain_id = 'Meas Value' "
   556→        "  AND standard_concept = 'S' "
   557→        "  AND LOWER(concept_name) = LOWER(:value_text) "
   558→        "LIMIT 1"
   559→    )
   560→    with engine.connect() as conn:
   561→        row = conn.execute(sql, {"value_text": key}).fetchone()
   562→        if row is not None:
   563→            return (row[1].lower(), int(row[0]))
   564→
   565→        # Try synonym match
   566→        sql_syn = text(
   567→            "SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name "
   568→            "FROM concept_synonym s "
   569→            "JOIN concept c ON s.concept_id = c.concept_id "
   570→            "WHERE c.domain_id = 'Meas Value' "
   571→            "  AND c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   572→            "  AND LOWER(s.concept_synonym_name) = LOWER(:value_text) "
   573→            "LIMIT 1"
   574→        )
   575→        row = conn.execute(sql_syn, {"value_text": key}).fetchone()
   576→        if row is not None:
   577→            return (row[1].lower(), int(row[0]))
   578→
   579→    return (None, None)
   580→
   581→
   582→def _lookup_ordinal_concept(engine: Any, scale_name: str, grade: str) -> int | None:
   583→    """Query concept + concept_synonym for a scale+grade combination.
   584→
   585→    Searches for ordinal scale values (e.g. "ECOG 2", "NYHA class III")
   586→    in the OMOP vocabulary.
   587→
   588→    Args:
   589→        engine: SQLAlchemy engine for the OMOP vocabulary database.
   590→        scale_name: Canonical scale name (e.g. "ecog", "karnofsky").
   591→        grade: Grade/level value (e.g. "2", "80").
   592→
   593→    Returns:
   594→        omop_concept_id or None if not found.
   595→    """
   596→    # Build search patterns for the scale + grade combo
   597→    patterns = [
   598→        f"{scale_name} {grade}",
   599→        f"{scale_name} grade {grade}",
   600→        f"{scale_name} performance status {grade}",
   601→        f"{scale_name} score {grade}",
   602→        f"{scale_name} class {grade}",
   603→    ]
   604→
   605→    for pattern in patterns:
   606→        sql = text(
   607→            "SELECT c.concept_id "
   608→            "FROM concept c "
   609→            "WHERE c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   610→            "  AND LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE LOWER(:pattern) "
   611→            "LIMIT 1"
   612→        )
   613→        with engine.connect() as conn:
   614→            row = conn.execute(sql, {"pattern": f"%{pattern}%"}).fetchone()
   615→            if row is not None:
   616→                return int(row[0])
   617→
   618→        # Try synonyms
   619→        sql_syn = text(
   620→            "SELECT c.concept_id "
   621→            "FROM concept_synonym s "
   622→            "JOIN concept c ON s.concept_id = c.concept_id "
   623→            "WHERE c.standard_concept = 'S' "
   624→            "  AND LOWER(s.concept_synonym_name) LIKE LOWER(:pattern) "
   625→            "LIMIT 1"
   626→        )
   627→        with engine.connect() as conn:
   628→            row = conn.execute(sql_syn, {"pattern": f"%{pattern}%"}).fetchone()
   629→            if row is not None:
   630→                return int(row[0])
   631→
   632→    return None
   633→
   634→
   635→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   636→# Public async API
   637→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   638→
   639→
   640→async def lookup_omop_concept(
   641→    entity_text: str,
   642→    entity_type: str,
   643→    *,
   644→    is_acronym: bool = False,
   645→) -> OmopLookupResult:
   646→    """Look up the best OMOP standard concept for a medical entity.
   647→
   648→    Maps the entity type to OMOP domain filters (primary + fallback),
   649→    queries the concept and concept_synonym tables in the OMOP vocabulary
   650→    database, scores candidates with fuzzy string matching, and returns
   651→    the best result above the minimum similarity threshold.
   652→
   653→    The synchronous database I/O is executed in a thread-pool executor to
   654→    avoid blocking the async event loop.
   655→
   656→    Requires OMOP_VOCAB_URL to be set. Raises RuntimeError if not configured.
   657→
   658→    Args:
   659→        entity_text: The medical entity text to look up (e.g. "metformin",
   660→            "type 2 diabetes mellitus", "hemoglobin A1c").
   661→        entity_type: Pipeline entity type used to determine the OMOP domain
   662→            filter. One of "Condition", "Medication", "Lab_Value",
   663→            "Procedure", "Demographic". Unknown types fall back to
   664→            "Observation".
   665→        is_acronym: If True, skip domain filter for synonym search
   666→            to find acronyms across all OMOP domains.
   667→
   668→    Returns:
   669→        OmopLookupResult with the best-matching OMOP concept, or an empty
   670→        result if no match is found above the similarity threshold.
   671→
   672→    Raises:
   673→        RuntimeError: If OMOP_VOCAB_URL is not set.
   674→    """
   675→    if not entity_text or not entity_text.strip():
   676→        raise ValueError("Empty entity_text passed to lookup_omop_concept")
   677→
   678→    domain_ids = _get_domain_filters(entity_type)
   679→
   680→    logger.debug(
   681→        "OMOP lookup: entity='%s', type='%s', domains=%s, acronym=%s",
   682→        entity_text[:50],
   683→        entity_type,
   684→        domain_ids,
   685→        is_acronym,
   686→    )
   687→
   688→    result = await asyncio.to_thread(
   689→        _sync_lookup, entity_text, domain_ids, is_acronym=is_acronym
   690→    )
   691→
   692→    return result
   693→

data.prompt:
Design a plan for separating value from unit in the grounding golden test fixtures and linking units to medical terminology codes (UCUM, OMOP, and optionally UMLS/SNOMED).

## Context

The project is a clinical trial protocol analysis pipeline. The file `tests/e2e/test_snippets.json` contains golden examples for grounding validation. Currently, each grounding entity looks like:

```json
{
  "entity_name": "Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate",
  "system": "UMLS",
  "code": "C0858118",
  "relation": "<",
  "value": "45 ml/min"  // <-- unit embedded in value string
}
```

The user wants to:
1. Separate the numeric value from the unit in the golden examples
2. Link each unit to terminology codes (primarily UCUM + OMOP concept_id)
3. Plan the downstream impact across the rest of the app

## What Already Exists

### Backend (already separates value/unit):
- **`FieldMappingValue`** (`field_mapper.py:47-80`): Already has `type` discriminator with `value`, `unit`, `min`, `max`, `duration` fields
- **`FieldMappingItem`** (`field_mapper.py:88-122`): Has `value: FieldMappingValue` + `unit: str` + `value_concept_id` + `value_concept_system`
- **`AtomicCriterion`** (`shared/models.py:184-233`): Already has:
  - `value_numeric: float | None`
  - `value_text: str | None` 
  - `unit_text: str | None`
  - `unit_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP via UCUM)
  - `value_concept_id: int | None` (OMOP for categoricals)

### Unit Normalization (already links to OMOP):
- **`normalize_unit()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:78-94`): Returns `(ucum_code, omop_unit_concept_id)`
  - Known mappings: "%" → (%, 8554), "mg/dL" → (mg/dL, 8840), "years" → (a, 9448), "mL/min" → (mL/min, 8795), "kg/m2" → (kg/m2, 9531), "mL/min/1.73m2" → (mL/min/1.73m2, 720870), "{score}" → ({score}, 8527)
- **`normalize_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:118-136`): Categorical value lookup ("positive" → 45884084, "negative" → 45878583)
- **`normalize_ordinal_value()`** (`unit_normalizer.py:169-215`): Ordinal scale lookup, always returns unit_concept_id=8527 ({score})

### Exporters (already use unit_concept_id):
- **CIRCE exporter** (`circe_builder.py:200-214`): Exports `UnitConceptId` in ValueAsNumber filter
- **Evaluation SQL** (`evaluation_sql_builder.py:172-178`): Filters on `unit_concept_id`
- **FHIR exporter** (`fhir_group_builder.py:178-200`): Uses unit_text + UCUM system URI

### Frontend (already displays separate value/unit):
- **`FieldValue`** (`types.ts:19-38`): TypeScript discriminated union with StandardValue{value, unit}, RangeValue{min, max, unit}, TemporalValue{duration, unit}
- **`FieldMapping`** (`types.ts:41-48`): Has entity_code, entity_system, omop_concept_id
- **`ValueInput.tsx`**: Separate input fields for value and unit

1→"""Shared concept ID resolution for export builders.
     2→
     3→Centralizes the logic for resolving the best concept identifier
     4→from AtomicCriterion records, used by CIRCE, FHIR Group, and
     5→evaluation SQL builders.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from shared.models import AtomicCriterion
    11→
    12→
    13→def get_concept_id(atomic: AtomicCriterion) -> int | None:
    14→    """Get the best integer concept ID for an atomic criterion.
    15→
    16→    Prefers omop_concept_id, falls back to entity_concept_id.
    17→    Returns None if neither is a valid integer.
    18→
    19→    Args:
    20→        atomic: AtomicCriterion record.
    21→
    22→    Returns:
    23→        Integer concept ID, or None.
    24→    """
    25→    for val in (atomic.omop_concept_id, atomic.entity_concept_id):
    26→        if val is not None:
    27→            try:
    28→                return int(val)
    29→            except (ValueError, TypeError):
    30→                continue
    31→    return None
    32→
    33→
    34→def get_concept_code(atomic: AtomicCriterion) -> str | None:
    35→    """Get the best string concept code for an atomic criterion.
    36→
    37→    Prefers omop_concept_id, falls back to entity_concept_id.
    38→    Returns None if neither is available.
    39→
    40→    Args:
    41→        atomic: AtomicCriterion record.
    42→
    43→    Returns:
    44→        String concept code, or None.
    45→    """
    46→    for val in (atomic.omop_concept_id, atomic.entity_concept_id):
    47→        if val is not None:
    48→            return str(val)
    49→    return None
